headline: 12 dead, 300+ injured as Houthi attack hits Riyadh airport
summary: Two Bangladeshis are among the dead after Yemen's Houthi group targeted King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia.
details: A deadly attack by Yemen's Houthi group on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has left 12 people dead and over 300 injured.
Among the deceased are two Bangladeshi nationals, four Saudis, and citizens from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan, and Egypt.
The Bangladesh government has strongly condemned the attack, calling the targeting of civilian infrastructure and lives unacceptable.
The Bangladesh mission in Riyadh is currently coordinating with Saudi authorities to identify the victims and provide assistance to the affected.
This incident follows two other attacks on the same airport over the past week, which killed four people and damaged an aircraft.
The Houthis stated the strike is part of a broader campaign against Saudi Arabia that began this summer.
Bangladesh has reiterated its solidarity with Saudi Arabia and called for a peaceful resolution to the West Asian crisis through diplomacy.
caption:
12 dead and over 300 injured after a Houthi attack on Riyadh airport, including two Bangladeshis.

A deadly attack by Yemen's Houthi group on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has left 12 people dead and over 300 injured.

Among the deceased are two Bangladeshi nationals, four Saudis, and citizens from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan, and Egypt.

The Bangladesh government has strongly condemned the attack, calling the targeting of civilian infrastructure and lives unacceptable.

The Bangladesh mission in Riyadh is currently coordinating with Saudi authorities to identify the victims and provide assistance to the affected.

This incident follows two other attacks on the same airport over the past week, which killed four people and damaged an aircraft.

The Houthis stated the strike is part of a broader campaign against Saudi Arabia that began this summer.

Bangladesh has reiterated its solidarity with Saudi Arabia and called for a peaceful resolution to the West Asian crisis through diplomacy.

headline_marked: India court [[releases 'cockroach' movement leaders]] after mass detentions
headline: India court releases 'cockroach' movement leaders after mass detentions
summary: Abhijeet Dipke and two other CJP leaders were freed by a magistrate's court on the condition that they maintain peace for one year.
details: An executive magistrate's court in New Delhi has released Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, and Saurav Das, leaders of the youth-led 'cockroach' movement (Cockroach Janta Party - CJP).
The leaders were detained on Saturday to prevent a major protest against the head of the Election Commission of India (ECI) at the Jantar Mantar site.
Authorities conducted a sweeping security operation across the capital, detaining thousands of protesters to thwart the demonstration.
The protest was organized to demand the ECI chief's resignation over a nationwide voter-roll revision that allegedly removed over 133 million names.
While election authorities claim the revision aimed to remove fraudulent entries, critics argue it disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims.
The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights called for the immediate release of all those 'arbitrarily detained' in New Delhi.
Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and the CJP have vowed to continue their protests, with Gandhi stating that government crackdowns will only increase the anger of Gen Z and students.
caption:
Thousands detained, but the leaders are out. India's 'cockroach' movement leaders have been released by a court.

An executive magistrate's court in New Delhi has released Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, and Saurav Das, leaders of the youth-led 'cockroach' movement (Cockroach Janta Party - CJP).

The leaders were detained on Saturday to prevent a major protest against the head of the Election Commission of India (ECI) at the Jantar Mantar site.

Authorities conducted a sweeping security operation across the capital, detaining thousands of protesters to thwart the demonstration.

The protest was organized to demand the ECI chief's resignation over a nationwide voter-roll revision that allegedly removed over 133 million names.

While election authorities claim the revision aimed to remove fraudulent entries, critics argue it disproportionately affected minorities, particularly Muslims.

The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights called for the immediate release of all those 'arbitrarily detained' in New Delhi.

Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and the CJP have vowed to continue their protests, with Gandhi stating that government crackdowns will only increase the anger of Gen Z and students.
